title: Nucleic Acid Extraction Protocol for Recalcitrant Species
author: Lilian P Matallana Ramirez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5pwg5pe

steps.title: Settle ground tissue
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the ground tissue to pull it down and prevent it from blocking buffer flow, then clean gloves to avoid cross‑contamination.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 1000 × g for 30 s (temperature not specified).
For RNA samples, centrifuge at 1000 rpm, 4 °C for 15 s.
Open tubes carefully, remove strip caps or sealing mat, and clean gloves with tissues and 75 % ethanol.
Optional: use a single toothpick per sample to pull down tissue instead of centrifugation.

steps.title: Add lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Introduce 600 µL of the appropriate lysis buffer to each sample, keeping reagents on ice or pre‑warmed as required, and close the tubes.

substeps.instruction: Add 600 µL lysis buffer to each tube.
For RNA, place minitube plates on ice for 1–2 min to thaw, keep LBR on ice, and ensure the buffer is liquid before adding.
For DNA, add pre‑warmed LBD at 60 °C.
Close tubes with strip caps.

steps.title: Homogenize lysate
steps.instruction: Shake the plates in a Tissue Lyser to obtain a homogeneous lysate, add sarkosyl for RNA, and perform the incubation cycle.

substeps.instruction: Homogenize in Tissue Lyser: DNA 4–6 min at 25 Hz; RNA 3 min at 25 Hz.
Keep plates and adaptors on ice during shaking.
While shaking, prepare a second set of 192 clean 1.1 mL tubes in two plates for later transfer.
For RNA, add 10 µL of 20 % sarkosyl per 1 mL lysate and keep plates at 4 °C.
For DNA, optionally extend this step for samples >2 years old in silica gel or with high phenol content.
After adding LBD, shake plates 5 min at 25 Hz.
Incubate at 65 °C for 30 min; repeat this incubation 3 times (total 1.5 h).
Centrifuge plates at 5 000 rpm, 4 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Settle lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge briefly to collect the lysate at the bottom of the tubes and keep the work area clean.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge plates at 1000 × g for 30 s to settle liquid.
For RNA samples, place tubes on ice after centrifugation.
Remove caps and clean gloves between rows.

steps.title: Transfer lysate and fresh buffer
steps.instruction: Move a defined volume of lysate to clean tubes and bring the total volume up to 1 mL with fresh lysis buffer.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 400–600 µL lysate to a new clean set of tubes (step 1.3).
Add fresh LBD (DNA) or LBR (RNA) up to a final volume of 1 mL.
For RNA, note that the tubes may already contain 10 µL of 20 % sarkosyl.
Adjust volume up or down depending on tissue type to improve yield.

steps.title: Incubate and spin
steps.instruction: Heat the lysate briefly, cool, and then centrifuge to remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 65 °C for 10 min, flipping the plate gently every 5 min.
Cool on ice for ~10 min.
Centrifuge at 5 000 rpm, 4 °C for 1 min.

steps.title: Wash with WB
steps.instruction: Perform two washes with wash buffer to clean the nucleic acids.

substeps.instruction: Add 750 µL wash buffer (WB) to each sample.
Spin for 1 min and discard the flow‑through.
Repeat the wash step a total of two times.

steps.title: Protein wash
steps.instruction: Apply protein wash buffer twice, ensuring complete removal of liquid without exceeding recommended spin times.

substeps.instruction: Add 600 µL protein wash buffer (PWB) to each sample.
Spin for 1 min and discard the flow‑through.
Repeat the protein wash step a total of two times.
If needed, spin an additional up to 2 min until all liquid passes, but do not exceed 3 min total.

steps.title: Final spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge briefly to eliminate any remaining liquid through the glass‑fiber filter.

substeps.instruction: Spin plates for 1–2 min.
If necessary, extend by another 2 min, but never exceed 5 min total.

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation / organic extraction
steps.instruction: Mix lysate with ethanol (or chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol for DNA) and centrifuge to precipitate nucleic acids.

substeps.instruction: In a new empty deep‑well plate, combine 900 µL 95 % ethanol with 600 µL lysate from step 1.6 and mix with a multichannel pipette.
Alternative for DNA: combine 400 µL lysate (step 1.3) with 600 µL chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1).
Close tubes with strip caps.
Invert plates gently ~20 times by hand.
Centrifuge at 5 000 rpm, 4 °C for 10 min.
Wear a gas mask and handle chloroform in a fume hood; avoid plastic containers.

steps.title: Bind lysate to PALL plate
steps.instruction: Transfer lysate to the PALL filter plate and freeze to promote binding.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 600 µL lysate (from step 2.1) to the PALL plate.
Cover the PALL plate with an air‑pore tape sheet.
Place the plate in a –20 °C freezer for at least 45 min (30–60 min optimal).
Alternative for DNA: transfer 150–200 µL clear supernatant to the PALL plate and add 500–600 µL cold 95 % ethanol.
Carefully remove only the top clear layer; avoid disturbing lower layers.
Cover and freeze as above.

steps.title: Prepare plates and accessories
steps.instruction: Set up all deep‑well, PALL, PCR plates and sealing materials, keeping labels consistent.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 96‑deep‑well plates, air‑pore tape sheets, PALL plates, PCR plates, and sealing foils/strip caps for PCR plates.
Keep the same labels and marks used for the minitube plates.
Minimize spinning times to protect the glass‑fiber filter quality.
If a small amount of liquid remains in wells, discard it quickly by flipping the plate before the next wash.

steps.title: Assemble PALL on PCR plate
steps.instruction: Stack the PALL filter plate onto the PCR plate, ensuring proper alignment.

substeps.instruction: Place the PALL plate on top of the PCR plate.
Label the plate properly and verify that each position matches (e.g., A1 on PALL aligns with A1 on PCR).

steps.title: Centrifuge and dry plates
steps.instruction: Spin the assembled plates briefly and allow them to dry under controlled conditions.

substeps.instruction: Spin plates for 1 min.
Hold at room temperature in the hood for 5 min.
For RNA samples, keep plates on ice while drying.

steps.title: Optional DNase/RNase treatment and QC
steps.instruction: Perform optional enzymatic cleanup and assess nucleic‑acid quality.

substeps.instruction: Add DNase or RNase (using filtered tips) if downstream applications require it; handle enzymes carefully to avoid contamination.
Measure nucleic‑acid concentration and purity with a NanoDrop 2000 spectrophotometer.
Assess integrity on an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer with Pico chips.

steps.title: Cleanup with kits
steps.instruction: Purify and concentrate the extracted nucleic acids using appropriate commercial kits.

substeps.instruction: For RNA, use the Zymo Research RNA Clean & Concentrator‑5™ kit.
For DNA, select a suitable cleanup kit based on downstream needs.

steps.title: Elute nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Recover purified DNA or RNA in a small volume of appropriate elution buffer.

substeps.instruction: Elute DNA with 20–40 µL AE buffer pre‑heated to 50 °C; incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Elute RNA with 20–40 µL molecular‑grade water (RNase/DNase‑free); incubate 2 min on ice.
Spin plates for 1 min to collect eluate.

steps.title: Seal and store plates
steps.instruction: Cover the plates securely and store them at appropriate temperatures.

substeps.instruction: Cover each plate with a sealing foil or 8‑strip caps.
Store RNA plates at –80 °C.
Store DNA plates at –20 °C or –80 °C for long‑term storage.
